cases.evidence: piece used a wrong subject before India arrived
cases.proposed_rule: Do not close a fronted clause until its subject is explicit.

example_pair.input: But, after losing the captain's wicket India only made 36 runs loosing 7 wickets to end the innings.
example_pair.output: But, after losing the captain's wicket India <SEG:1> only made 36 runs <SEG:2> loosing 7 wickets to end the innings.

cases.span: hard for primates like us to digest
cases.evidence: split adjective from its to-infinitive; got read as purpose
cases.proposed_rule: Keep 'hard/difficult to VERB' together; do not split the adjective from its infinitive.

example_pair.input: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
example_pair.output: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest <SEG:1> unless they are cooked.

cases.span: as member of the Buenos Aires province
cases.evidence: piece ended before the head noun 'delegation'
cases.proposed_rule: Do not split inside an appositive or role phrase before its head noun arrives.

example_pair.input: Mrs. Kirchner announced her intention to run for president at the Argentine Theatre, the same location she used to start her 2005 campaign for the Senate as member of the Buenos Aires province delegation.
example_pair.output: Mrs. Kirchner announced her intention to run for president at the Argentine Theatre, the same location she used to start her 2005 campaign for the Senate as member of the Buenos Aires province delegation <SEG:1>.

cases.evidence: temporal modifier was split off from the quantified noun phrase
cases.proposed_rule: Keep quantified noun phrases intact until their restrictive modifiers are present.

example_pair.input: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa.
example_pair.output: However, the percentage of XDR-TB in the entire group of people with tuberculosis still seems to be low; 6,000 of the total 330,000 people infected at any particular moment in South Africa <SEG:1>.

cases.evidence: boundary came before the technical head noun was complete
cases.proposed_rule: Keep technical compounds with their head noun; do not break after a bare modifier.

example_pair.input: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical.
example_pair.output: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions <SEG:1> in the tested chemical.

summary: The prompt most often cuts before the controlling subject or head noun is available, so fronted clauses, appositive role phrases, quantified NPs, and technical compounds get translated with the wrong attachment. It also splits adjective+infinitive predicates too early, which turns a difficulty statement into a purpose/ability reading.
